results.title: An unbranded Category view has no KPI cards and follows the Overview rules at category scope

steps.title: Given the user opens analysis UA
When the user opens category C1 in the sidebar
Then there are no KPI cards
And InBrief and Top Topics follow the topic rules at category scope
And the SOV ring and rankings are neutral

results.notes: Analysis used: UA = Electric bikes (42c3ab89), C1 = Commuter Electric Bikes, latest collection 21 Oct 2026 (2 collections now: 20 and 21 Oct), GB only (topic Electric bikes instead of Postal services, no C2 / FR). Overview displayed, then category view. No KPI card (Visibility / Avg Position / AI Choice / Sentiment cards absent; headings = Top Topics in the Category, Share of Voice, Brand Prioritization, Commuter Electric Bikes landscape, AI Engines Citation Sources) and no 'vs previous period' delta. InBrief (logo image 'InBrief powered by AI Sense') shows 3 bullets about C1 (motor type Bosch/Shimano mid-drive; practical features mudguards/lights/racks for daily commuting; battery capacity 250Wh+ Panasonic/Samsung/Sony) with caption 'Category summary generated by artificial intelligence'. 'Top Topics in the Category' lists 7 C1 topics (practical features, motor type, battery capacity, puncture-resistant tyres, comfort and usability, build quality, legal compliance), no brand. SOV ring: 11 slices with the same stroke and no slice larger than the outer radius, no centre value; API isTargetBrand=false for every brand. Landscape rows all white background / weight 400, no highlighted row. First-run findings: SOV legend rounding still present (API 22.5 -> 23% and 7.5 -> 8%, legend sums to 101%); aria-label 'Perception topics' on the topics list still present.

results.notes: Analysis used: UA = Electric bikes (42c3ab89), C1 = Commuter Electric Bikes, latest collection 21 Oct 2026, market United Kingdom (GB only, fixed market label = GB (EN)). Quadrants Stars, Opportunity, At Risk and Monitor shown, badge '5 brands'. SOV ring of C1 (API sov-distribution): Specialized 22.5, Carrera 10, Ribble 10, Tern 10, MiRider 7.5, then Cube / Gazelle / Scott / Tenways / Vello 5. Matrix (API brand-matrix, 1 point per brand, en-GB): Specialized, Ribble, Tern, Carrera, MiRider = exactly the top 5 of the ring; the 5th place is no longer a tie (7.5 vs 5), so the first-run PARTIAL is lifted. No target: isTargetBrand=false on every point, no '(Target)' label, no target style in the matrix markup. First-run findings: (1) quadrant mismatch still present - the UI counts the 5 brands in 'At Risk' (and labels MiRider 'AT RISK') while the API returns quadrant 'MONITOR' for all 5 (quadrantCounts monitor=5, atRisk=0); (2) expanded cluster still spills outside the plot area - Tern drawn below the 0% axis and the 5th dot (Ribble) at x=1254 px beyond the plot right edge (1239 px), unlabelled; Specialized is drawn at about 20% AI choice although its winRate is 0 (cluster spread). Top-5 tie-break PO question: not exercisable today (no tie), still open.

results.title: Time Evolution still needs 7 collections in the window

steps.title: Given the user opens category C1 of analysis UA
When the user selects a window with fewer than 7 collections
Then the chart is not available

results.notes: Analysis used: UA = Electric bikes (42c3ab89), C1 = Commuter Electric Bikes, 2 collections (20 and 21 Oct 2026). Windows with fewer than 7 collections selected (filter only, not saved): Last 7 days (2 collections) and All reports (2 collections): Time Evolution is not rendered at all (no widget, no 'Not enough data' text). Production references (read only, same windows): Nike brand category (3 collections) Last 7 days - Time Evolution not rendered either; BYD brand category Last 7 days (16-22 Oct = 6 collections) - not rendered; BYD brand category / Overview Last 30 days (27 collections) - Time Evolution rendered. So UA behaves like production for a window with fewer than 7 collections (widget hidden). PARTIAL because (1) the expected wording 'shows the same "not enough data" state' does not match the production state observed today (hidden, not a 'Not enough data' card) and (2) UA never reached 7 collections, so 'hidden because of the 7-collection rule' cannot be told apart from 'never shown on unbranded categories'. First-run BYD finding (7 daily dates in Last 7 days still said 'At least 7 report runs are needed'): changed - with Last 30 days (27 collections) the card first shows 'Not enough data / At least 7 report runs are needed to show trends.' while loading, then the chart renders (transient flash, still worth a note to dev); with Last 7 days (6 collections today) the widget is hidden. Side observation (brand, out of scope): the BYD lines stop around 5-9 Oct although collections exist up to 21 Oct.
results.gap_type: missing data (UA < 7 collections) + CSV gap (expected 'not enough data' state vs production hidden widget)

Then its row also shows "Split"

results.notes: Analysis used: UA2 = bike (d3fd1b30), C1 = Mountain Bikes, latest collection 22 Oct 2026, 2 engines (ChatGPT + Gemini); UA Electric bikes also scanned. Disagreement case: 'Which Mountain Bikes should I buy?' - ChatGPT 'Trek Fuel EXe was chosen', Gemini 'Specialized Stumpjumper was chosen' -> row Winner / Themes shows the 'Split' chip. 1 vs 1 only: every existing unbranded analysis has 2 engines, so '2 engines on A and 1 on B' cannot be built. API scan of every Visibility / Competitive prompt of UA2 (22 prompts) and UA (2 prompts, both collections): every engine returned a ranking (9 or 10 items, 4 for Competitive) - no empty ranking exists (the UA Other-type prompt has no ranking by design and shows themes). 'No ranking returned' never appears in the prompts table (13 'Split' chips, 0 'No ranking returned'). Consistency check: all 'Split' rows have different first brand families, all single-brand rows (Specialized x6) have the same family first for both engines. Same PARTIAL as the first run.
results.gap_type: missing data (no 3-engine unbranded analysis, no empty ranking) + CSV gap (allow 1 vs 1 with 2 engines)

results.title: The winner is computed per collection, not over the date range

steps.title: Given the user opens category C1 of analysis UA on the latest collection
When the user selects the earlier collection
Then prompt R shows the winner of that collection
When the user selects a date range covering both collections
Then the winner is not aggregated over the range

results.notes: Analyses used: UA = Electric bikes (C1 Commuter Electric Bikes, collections 20 and 21 Oct) and UA2 = bike (Mountain Bikes and Road Bikes, collections 21 and 22 Oct). API scan of every Visibility / Competitive prompt, per collection, with both engines and with each engine alone: no prompt has a different winner between the two collections (UA: both prompts 'Split' on both days; UA2: identical winners on 21 and 22 Oct, identical first-ranked items) - precondition 'prompt R' not met. UI steps still replayed on UA2 Mountain Bikes with 'Most popular Mountain Bikes?' (Specialized): 22 Oct -> 21 Oct -> All reports (21-22 Oct), the row shows 'Specialized' each time. Observation (to check with dev / PO, same in production): when the date is changed, the SOV / matrix / rankings / InBrief calls are re-sent with from/to, but no new prompts-table request (categories/{id}/questions) is sent - the table keeps the latest-collection data. Same on brand analysis Toyota (category 21a79173, 21 Oct -> 20 Oct: no questions request). If this is intended, 'winner of the selected collection' (AC-5 and step 'The prompts table reloads') can never be met; if not, it is a product bug also present in production.
